tasks.short: Monitor drilling conditions and judge adjustment needs.

steps.what: Monitor drilling operations by checking actual gauges and drilling conditions
Listen to actual drilling equipment and assess sound, vibration and operating behaviour
outputs: actual drilling sound and behaviour observations

steps.what: Determine whether drilling adjustments or equipment alterations are needed
inputs: actual drilling sound and behaviour observations

steps.what: Enter and check actual readings, observations and decisions in the drilling log {OPS_SYSTEM}
inputs: actual drilling sound and behaviour observations
outputs: checked final drilling observation log entry

steps.what: Save the checked actual drilling observation log entry
inputs: checked final drilling observation log entry
outputs: saved actual drilling observation log entry

tasks.design: Test native reuse of supported readings from the rig telemetry system {OTHER} in the existing drilling log {OPS_SYSTEM}. The driller still checks gauges, listens, judges adjustment needs and manually captures actual sound and decision notes; only repeated numerical and rig-reference entry may shrink.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual gauge values and rig references can be typed again in a drilling log.
tasks.enabler_now: Native log fields can reuse actual rig telemetry where compatible and already produced.
tasks.still_hard: Noise, vibration, ground changes and unusual gauge behaviour need an attentive driller.
tasks.human_edge: The driller recognises an unsafe or unusual drilling condition and decides whether work needs changing.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring and adjustment decisions stay unchanged; a small part of existing log entry can shrink.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: some drilling rigs provide timestamped telemetry that can be reused in existing logs; compatibility and local availability must be verified, and telemetry does not replace listening or operating judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring and determining adjustment needs through the actual existing log, not executing an equipment alteration. If no log is written, remove its shares and reweight rather than creating paperwork.

Rig sensors produce actual rig identifier, timestamp, depth and supported pressure or speed readings during the operation observed in s1. Driller verifies correspondence in s4 and manually records actual noise, behaviour and the s3 decision. Missing or stale exports stay manual. Installing sensors or digitising unsupported gauges is not assumed free.

Test native log configuration before code. Existing telemetry runtime and already-populated log fields earn no saving. Only genuinely repeated numerical/reference entry changes; gauge checking, listening and judgement are fully retained.
Shares and reductions are provisional, not measured baselines. The final save is one percent fully retained and the existing entry check supplies its gate.
unknowns: Is a drilling log actually written for this work?
Do actual rigs export compatible readings?
What log fields are already populated?
research_questions: Does native reading reuse remove repeated entry after all timestamp and rig checks are counted?

incremental.description: Maintain rig-to-log field configuration and check changed telemetry formats.

approvals.approved_version: s4 checked final drilling observation log entry, exact rig, time and log destination; edits require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 4*0.50 repeated log fields = 2; minus 0.5 upkeep = 1.5. If half the readings can be reused, 1 minus 0.5 = 0.5. All physical monitoring and judgement remain unchanged; existing telemetry runtime supplies no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The driller's monitoring and operating decisions stay unchanged; only repeated fields in actual logs can shrink.
role.ambitious_version: No operating rights change; verify whether actual log re-entry is large enough to justify configuration.
